answer: Make each epoch's proof memory-CAPACITY-hard: it needs a large RAM working set held all at once, and every identity's proof is due inside one tight beacon-timed window, so the work cannot be time-sliced. One honest agent fills one block of memory, solid as onyx. An operator running a thousand personas on a host must hold a thousand working sets at the same instant — no taking turns, since all deadlines strike together — so DRAM cost climbs linearly with the fake count. The old fable of one machine minting endless identities hits a hard hardware ledge.
